note.text: A rock is an aggregate of minerals or other natural solid material. Igneous rocks form when molten material cools and solidifies. Sedimentary rocks form through accumulation and consolidation of sediment, or other sedimentary processes. Metamorphic rocks form when existing rock changes under heat, pressure or fluids without melting completely. The rock cycle links formation, weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, change and melting. It has several pathways, not one compulsory route for every rock.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A rock is an aggregate of minerals or other natural solid material. Igneous rocks form when molten material cools and solidifies. Sedimentary rocks form through accumulation and consolidation of sediment, or other sedimentary processes. Metamorphic rocks form when existing rock changes under heat, pressure or fluids without melting completely. The rock cycle links formation, weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, change and melting. It has several pathways, not one compulsory route for every rock.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A Cameroonian class may compare basalt from a volcanic area with layered sedimentary material and a metamorphic sample supplied by a teacher. Observation helps suggest a classification, but colour alone is not decisive. Ask about texture, minerals and how the sample formed. A rock can pass through several changes over long geological times.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Classify by formation, then use observations as supporting evidence. Do not call any heated rock igneous unless melting and solidification are involved. Distinguish transport from deposition: moving material and laying it down are different stages.
